AgentsSettings.description: How far and how wide delegation to sub-agents may go.

max_concurrent.description:
Sub-agents the model may have running at once anywhere under one
session — foreground, background and resumed ones, at every depth.
A spawn beyond it is refused with a message telling the model to wait
or do the work itself. `TeamCreate` members and persistent team
members have their own limits (`team.*`) and do not count.

max_depth.description:
How many delegations deep a chain of sub-agents may go: a session a
host created is depth 0, and an agent at this depth is not offered
the `Agent` tool. Applies to team members too.

AppSettings.description:
What is decided once for the whole instance: read from the global tier's
files only (and from what an embedder sets in memory), never from a scene
or a project.

history.description:
Where sessions are kept. `global` (default): under the state root's
`projects/` and `sessions/`. `project`: a session of a trusted project
goes to that project's `<project dir>/state/history/<id>/` (a
worktree's to its main checkout's), with only an index under
`sessions/<id>/`; the rest stay global. What is already kept either
way is read where it is, and history kept in a project is read only
while the project is trusted. Takes effect when the daemon starts.

session_cap.description:
How many sessions the daemon keeps in memory. Creating or bringing
back one more takes the least recently active idle session out of
memory; its transcript stays and the next use brings it back. Takes
effect when the daemon starts; `config.reload` does not apply a change.

system_proxy.description:
The engine's own HTTP (model calls, `WebFetch` / `Ping`, MCP over
HTTP, OAuth) follows `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY` /
`NO_PROXY` from the environment (default). `false` connects directly,
ignoring them. Requests to this machine are direct either way. Not the
network of a sandboxed command, which `sandbox.network` decides. Takes
effect when the daemon starts; `config.reload` does not apply a change.

trust_all_projects.description: Trust every project no `trusted_projects` entry names.

trusted_projects.description:
Projects whose own configuration takes effect as written — see
`settings::trust`. Absolute paths, or globs where `*` stays within one
path segment and `**` crosses them; a leading `~/` is the home
directory. The global `settings.json` and `settings.local.json` lists
add up rather than one replacing the other; `project.trust` writes to
the second.

worker_threads.description:
`agixd`'s async worker threads, at least 1; unset, one per CPU core.
Blocking work (file I/O, searches, scripts) runs on a pool of its own
whatever this is. Read once, before `agixd` starts anything else;
`config.reload` does not apply a change. An embedded engine runs on
its host's runtime and does not read it.

worktree_dir.description:
The directory at a repository's root the engine's git worktrees go
in, which is also the line it adds to that repository's `.gitignore`:
one path component starting with `.`, not starting with `.git`, not a
configuration root nor another tool's directory
(`base::paths::Layout::with_worktrees_dir`). Unset, `.wkts`. A name
that is not allowed is ignored with a warning.

enabled.description:
`false`: the file tools write without recording what they overwrite,
and the session cannot rewind files.

max_bytes_per_file.description: A file larger than this is hashed but its earlier contents are not kept.

max_total_bytes.description:
Over this many bytes of kept copies per session, the oldest are
deleted and a `pruned` line is written to the transcript.

CompactionConfig.description:
Context compaction, over what the scene asks for. A field left out keeps
the scene's own value (`SceneSpec::token_budget`).

clear_on_cache_expiry.description:
Once an hour — the lifetime of the provider's prompt cache — blank all
but the 20 newest tool results and send the provider `cache_edits`
for the ones it still holds.

inline_result_chars.description:
A tool result longer than this many characters is saved to a file in
the project's `state/tool-results/` and the model gets its head, its
tail and the path (default 30,000; `0` keeps every result in the
conversation).
`Read`, `WebFetch` and `TaskOutput` page their own results and are
never saved.

keep_recent.description: How many recent rounds compaction leaves as they are.

reactive.description:
Clear old tool results early, in the middle of a turn: once fewer than
50,000 tokens are left below the threshold, or the context grows fast
enough to reach it within three model calls, the results of file,
shell and search tools older than the last `keep_recent` rounds (at
least five) are blanked — a `MicroCompact`, reported as a `compact`
event. Stops for the session after three passes in a row that freed
nothing.

threshold_tokens.description:
Compact once a request's context passes this many tokens. `0` turns
automatic compaction off.

Divergence.description:
What replay does when a live request differs from the one recorded at the
same position.

oneOf.description:
Fail the call, naming the fields that differ. The default wherever a
divergence means a broken test.
Report the difference and play the recorded response anyway.

Effort.description:
How much work the model puts into a reply. DeepSeek accepts `low`,
`high` and `max`, folding `medium` and `xhigh` into `high`.

http.description: An HTTP proxy that takes `CONNECT`, as `ip:port` or `localhost:port`.

no_proxy.description:
`NO_PROXY` for the command. Empty — the default — is set as empty, so
even `localhost` goes through the proxy; the sandbox lets nothing past
it either way.

socks.description:
A SOCKS5 proxy for `ALL_PROXY`, written the same way; its port must
differ from `http`'s.

FilesSettings.description: Where the tools may read and write beyond the project.

allow_write.description:
Paths to re-allow writing, on top of the built-in deny defaults. Most
specific wins.

The write-side counterpart of `sandbox.allow_read`, and it exists for
the same reason: the defaults sit on real workflows. A project that
keeps a checked-in `.env.example`, or a deployment whose agent is
meant to maintain a private-registry `.npmrc`, has to be able to say
"that one is fine here".

This exempts a path from the *deny* rules only. Where a tool may write
at all is a different question, answered by `extra_dirs` — keeping
them apart is what stops one setting quietly widening the project
boundary.

deny_write.description:
Extra filename segments a tool may never write, on top of the built-in
credential defaults (`.env`, `id_rsa`, `.ssh`, `.npmrc`, ...). A path is
refused if *any* of its components matches one, or begins with one
followed by a dot — so `.env` also covers `.env.production`. A
sandboxed `Bash` / `Monitor` command is held to the same names inside
its writable roots (on Linux only for entries that already exist).

extra_dirs.description:
Directories outside the project that tools may read and write, as if
they were part of it. The instance's own state directory (`~/.agix`
by default) is always readable, but only its `scratchpad` and
`memory` directories are writable this way.

read_dirs.description:
Directories outside the project that the file tools (`Read`, `Glob`,
`Grep`) and read-only shell commands may read without asking. `"/"`
lets them read anywhere. Reading anywhere else needs a person's
approval, and an unattended session — one with nobody to approve — is
refused.

GoalSettings.description: What the model may give a goal it sets for itself.

max_rounds.description:
The most automatic rounds a goal the model sets or edits
(`GoalCreate`, `GoalUpdate`) may have; a larger `max_rounds` is
lowered to it. A goal a host sets is not held to it.

McpServerEntry.description:
One `mcp.servers` entry: a server's configuration (`mcp::config::McpServerConfig`,
read by the MCP module, which this crate cannot depend on), and whether it is on.

enabled.description:
Unset is on. `null` is a bad value rather than unset: it would
otherwise override a lower tier's `false` and read as on.

McpSettings.description: MCP servers, keyed by server name.

servers.description:
Tiers merge by name and field, so a higher tier can change one field
of a server a lower one declared. An entry holding nothing but
`enabled` declares nothing: it turns off, or back on, the server of
that name declared in a lower tier or by a plugin — except in a
project that is not trusted, which may only turn servers off.

`$VAR` / `${VAR}` / `${VAR:-default}` are expanded in a server's
`command`, `args`, `env`, `url` and `headers` when it connects — the
only place in settings that expands anything. Every variable of the
daemon's environment read there, and every `*_env` of a server's
`oauth` block, counts as that server's secret: no other child process
inherits it (`sandbox.env`).

enabled.description:
The file-based memory system (`MEMORY.md` + one `.md` per memory).
Default `true`. `false` drops the memory prompt, the memory index in
each turn's reminder, and recall.

ModelSettings.description: Which providers model calls go to, and how they are made.

effort.description: Sent as `output_config.effort`; `None` leaves it to the endpoint.

order.description:
Provider ids, from `providers`, in the order a model call tries them:
the first is the default, and a call goes to the next when one is out
of quota, has no key, refuses the key, or cannot be reached once its
retries are spent. Every call starts from the first again. Each id must
be defined. Unset, the first defined provider alone.

tasks.description:
The tier — `strong`, `balanced` or `fast` — each kind of model call
asks the provider for.

ModelSpec.description:
A model with what the engine should know about it beyond its id.

`context_window` and `max_output` are applied to the model's calls;
`reasoning_levels` and `input_types` are kept and reported; nothing in
the engine decides by them.

max_output.description:
The most `max_tokens` a call to this model is sent with, and the most
a reply cut off at its limit is retried with. Unset, the model's
documented limit, looked up by its id.

oneOf.description: Unrestricted outbound (default; Bash often needs `curl` / `npm install`).

No outbound network access at all. On macOS 26 that includes name
resolution, which goes through `mDNSResponder`'s unix socket.

Outbound restricted to `SandboxPolicy::allowed_domains`. Neither
backend can filter by domain: macOS lets through localhost when the
list names it and nothing else, Linux cuts the network entirely, and
both report the domains they could not allow as unmet.

Outbound only to [`SandboxPolicy::egress_proxy`], with the command's
`*_PROXY` variables pointing at it; what the proxy lets through is the
proxy's business. Without an `egress_proxy` the network is cut, as
under `DenyAll`, and reported unmet.

PathStyle.description:
How file tools word the paths the model reads: in tool descriptions and in
the paths Grep, Glob, Write and Edit print. Resolving a path the model
passes in is the same in both styles (relative against the working
directory, absolute as is).

oneOf.description: Prompt user for each tool call that isn't explicitly allowed.

Allow file writes inside the project (the working directory and
`files.extra_dirs`) and read-only calls without asking;
ask about the rest, as `default` does. Writes into the project's
`.git`, its project directory (`.agix` unless renamed; then `.agix`
too), `.claude` and `.agents/skills` still ask.

Ask nothing and skip the rules of the user's tiers. Credentials
(`.ssh`, `.aws`, `.gnupg`, the state directory's settings and tokens)
are still refused, the deployment's managed `deny` / `ask` rules still
apply, input that is not valid is still refused, and `Bash` still runs
in the OS sandbox.
Plan mode — only allow read-only tools.
Don't ask — deny any tool not explicitly allowed (no prompt).

PermissionsSettings.description:
`permissions` in a settings file.

The rule lists are not merged like the rest: every tier's apply side by
side, a project's added to the global and scene ones, never substituted
for them; the merged settings hold none of them.

allow.description:
Rules that allow a call without asking: `Bash`, `Bash(git status:*)`,
`Read(~/notes/**)`, `mcp__server__tool`.

allow_exact.description:
Allow rules whose content is compared as written, not read as a
pattern: `Bash(rm a*.tmp)` allows that command and no other. "Allow
every time" records its answers here.

ask.description: Rules that ask before a call, even one an allow rule covers.

client_may_loosen.description:
Whether an RPC client may ask for *looser* settings than these — a more
permissive `mode` above, higher limits, allow rules.

The daemon's `session.create` takes the session's own settings in
`options.settings`. With this `false` — the default — a client can
*tighten* them, but a looser value is clamped to what is configured
here (`clamped_options`). Otherwise any client that could authenticate
could open a `bypassPermissions` session no matter how the daemon was
configured (`crates/assembly/src/server/mod.rs` notes there is no
per-method authorization on that socket).

Set it to `true` only when every client of this daemon is as trusted
as the daemon itself.

deny.description: Rules that refuse a call. A deny wins over any allow or ask.

prompt_timeout_secs.description:
How long a tool call waits for a host to answer a permission prompt
before the call is denied. `0` waits indefinitely (only session
cancellation interrupts it).

The wait itself lives in the engine (`execute_tool_inner`), so the
bound has to be reachable from `EngineConfig`, not only from a
daemon-side flag — a host driving the engine directly needs it too.

Failing closed (deny, not permit) on expiry is deliberate: a prompt
that went unanswered is not consent.

PluginsConfig.description:
Runtime control over the plugin subsystem, for a build that has it
compiled in.

The compile-time feature decides whether plugins *can* exist; this
decides whether they may. A deployment that wants none should prefer the
feature, since that leaves nothing to switch back on — this is for the
case where the same binary serves several deployments.

allow.description:
When non-empty, only these plugin names load. An allow-list, so a
name that is not on it is refused rather than merely unmentioned.

enable_on_install.description:
Whether `plugin.install` turns a package on once it is installed.
Off by default: the host reads the disclosure the install returns and
calls `plugin.enable` itself. `true` enables it as part of the install.

PromptSettings.description: What the system prompt says, over what the scene gives it.

append.description: Appended to the end of the system prompt.

instruction_files.description:
More instruction files (e.g. a `CLAUDE.md` outside the project), read
in order when the session is built and given to the model alongside
the discovered `AGENTS.md` files. A root session with a `FileChanged`
hook watches them.

override.description: Overrides the entire system prompt if set.

path_style.description:
How the file tools word paths for the model. `absolute` keeps
today's text; `relative` makes tool descriptions say paths are
relative to the working directory and prints Grep / Glob / Write /
Edit paths under it relative, so a recorded session replays in another
working directory and long paths stop repeating in every call.
Resolving paths is unchanged. Unset, the scene decides
(`SceneSpec::path_style`: `harnix` is relative, the rest absolute).

api.description:
`anthropic` (default), `openai_chat` or `openai_responses`, or a
protocol the host registered.

api_key_env.description:
The environment variable holding the key. Without one the host's
credential source is asked. No child process inherits it once a
settings file names it, unless `sandbox.env.allow` does.

base_url.description:
Required for `openai_chat`; `anthropic` without one uses Anthropic's
own API, `openai_responses` OpenAI's.

id.description:
Unique, of ASCII letters, digits, `-` and `_`. When the tiers define
the same id twice, the first in load order (global, scene, project;
each tier's `settings.local.json` after its `settings.json`) is used
and the rest ignored.

models.description:
The models this provider serves, each an id or an object with what
the engine should know about it. Empty accepts any id. Not fetched
from the provider — `config.listModels` does that, on request.

quota.description:
Token limits; past one, the provider is skipped until the period
turns over.

tiers.description:
Which model serves `strong`, `balanced` and `fast`. `strong` is
required; `balanced` defaults to `strong`'s, `fast` to `balanced`'s.
Each must be in `models` when `models` lists any.

vendor.description:
`anthropic`, `openai`, `deepseek`, `qwen`, `vllm`, `sglang` or
`generic` (default). Decides how thinking is switched, whether
reasoning is sent back and how effort is spelled.

Quota.description:
Token limits per period, counted as uncached input plus cache writes plus
output; cache reads do not count. A period left out has no limit.

RecorderConfig.description:
Recorder (record/replay) configuration. `None` on [`Settings`] leaves the
model wrapper a pass-through.

name.description:
Directory name for this recording under `root`. `None` uses the session
id, which is what production recording wants; tests name theirs so a
replay can find it again.

root.description:
Where recordings live. Each one is a self-contained directory beneath
it, so a host retires a recording by deleting that directory.

oneOf.description:
Re-issue a recording's requests against a real provider.

The third mode exists because the other two cannot answer "what would
the model have said if the prompt were different". `Replay` never reads
a request's content — it compares blob *ids* and returns the recorded
response — so editing a blob changes nothing it observes. `Rerun` loads
the request back from the blobs (picking up any edit), sends it, and
reports how the new response differs from the recorded one.

SandboxConfig.description: The OS sandbox `Bash` / `Monitor` commands run in.

allow_read.description:
Paths to re-allow reading, on top of the built-in credential deny
defaults (`~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.npmrc`, ...). It re-allows exactly the
entry it names; a parent directory, or a path below a denied one,
changes nothing. Never a path a `Read(...)` deny rule names.

Exists because those defaults are applied to `Bash`, and some of them
sit on legitimate workflows — `npm install` against a private registry
reads `~/.npmrc`, `docker build` reads `~/.docker/config.json`.
This is the way to say "yes, that one is fine here".

cache_dirs.description:
Package and build caches outside the project that a sandboxed `Bash`
command may write — `pip`, `npm`, `cargo` and the like fail without
them. Grouped by toolchain; a settings file replaces one group by
naming it (`"python": []` drops it), adds a group under a new name, and
leaves the rest at their defaults. `~/` means the user's home. The file
tools do not get these.

deny_read.description:
Paths a sandboxed `Bash` / `Monitor` command may not read, added to
the built-in credential list (`~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.npmrc`, ...);
`allow_read` is how to let one of those through. The `Read(...)` deny
rules that name a file or a directory are added on top; one with any
other glob (`**/*.pem`) is not, so name its files here or deny them
with a `Bash(...)` rule.

enabled.description:
Run commands in the sandbox, in a build that has one.

Default: true. The backend is behind the `sandbox` compile-time
feature, which is on by default; a build without it has nothing to
turn off and this setting changes nothing in it. It is the runtime half
of a two-part answer — the build decides whether a sandbox exists, this
decides whether to use the one it has.

env.description:
The environment `Bash` / `Monitor` commands, command hooks and MCP
stdio servers start from, sandboxed or not. By default the host's
environment minus the engine's own credentials: `ANTHROPIC_*`,
`AGIX_DAEMON_TOKEN`, and every variable a setting names as holding a
secret — a provider's `api_key_env`, an MCP server's
`oauth.client_secret_env` / `oauth.private_key_jwt.key_env` and every
`$VAR` in its `command`, `args`, `env`, `url` or `headers` (outside
the project's own tier), a plugin's MCP servers likewise, the
enterprise IdP's `client_secret_env`. `"mode": "allowlist"` keeps only
`PATH`, `HOME`, the locale and a few others, plus whatever `allow`
names. An MCP server takes the policy of the settings it is declared
in, with its own `env` added on top: what it is given there it gets,
another server's secret it does not.

reap_on_close.description:
Stop, when a daemon session ends (closed, evicted, or the daemon
shutting down), every process group its commands started that is still
running — including services a command deliberately left in the
background. Off by default: such a service outlives the session.

require.description:
Refuse to run a sandboxed command when this build on this platform
cannot actually enforce the policy, instead of running it
unconstrained.

Two ways to be unable: the `sandbox` compile-time feature (on by
default) was turned off, so no backend was compiled at all, or it is
on and the platform's tool is missing. Both refuse here, and the
message says which.

Off by default, which is the historical behavior: on Linux without
`bwrap`, and on platforms with no backend at all, a command whose
policy cannot be honored runs anyway with a warning. That is a silent
downgrade from "constrained" to "unconstrained" — fine for a laptop,
not fine for a host that treats the sandbox as a boundary.

Turning it on makes such a command fail with an error naming the
missing backend. The default is `false` rather than `true` only
because flipping it would break every Linux box without bubblewrap
installed, and every Windows host, on upgrade.

unattended_needs_network_policy.description:
In an unattended session, a `Bash` / `Monitor` command nobody can be
asked about runs without an allow rule only when the sandbox fully
holds it and `network.mode` is not `unrestricted`: the sandbox holds
writes, and an open network is a way out it does not cover. On by
default; `false` drops the network condition, so a fully held command
runs under an open network too.

SandboxNetwork.description:
The network of a sandboxed command. Not the engine's own HTTP, which
`app.system_proxy` decides.

mode.description:
Outbound network policy for sandboxed `Bash` commands. `allowlist`
lets through what `web.allowed_domains` names, as far as the OS
sandbox can; `proxy` lets a command connect only to `proxy`, which
both OS backends hold; filtering by domain is then the proxy's job.
The engine's own `WebFetch` and `Ping` are not bound by it: they use
the engine's network, not the proxy.

proxy.description:
Under `mode: "proxy"`, the one address a sandboxed command may
connect to: `"127.0.0.1:3128"` for an HTTP proxy, or an object with
`http`, an optional `socks` and `no_proxy`. The command gets
`HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` (both cases)
pointing at it. Put the proxy on this machine: macOS can hold a proxy
elsewhere only to its port, and Linux needs `socat` to relay to it,
cutting the network entirely without one. Ignored in other modes.
Only sandboxed commands go through it: the engine's own `WebFetch` and
`Ping` use the engine's network, not this proxy, and are not held to
`web.allowed_domains`; filtering by domain is the host's proxy's job.

ScheduleSettings.description:
What the model may schedule for itself with `CronCreate`. Jobs a host
creates (`schedule.create`) are not held to these.

max_model_jobs.description:
The most jobs the model's own `CronCreate` calls may hold in a session
at once; one it deletes, or one that has fired its last, makes room.
`0`: the model schedules none.

min_model_interval_minutes.description:
The fewest minutes between two fires of a recurring job the model
schedules, over the seven days it lives. `1` adds nothing to the
cron expression's own once-a-minute resolution.

ScriptBinding.description:
One script, bound to one extension point.

```jsonc
"scripts": [
  { "path": ".agix/scripts/prompt.js", "point": "prompt.assemble", "entry": "onAssemble" }
]
```

The point is a catalog id — see `base::interface::catalog` and
`docs/extension_points.md`. A binding naming a point the engine does not
have, or one scripts may not use, is refused at startup with a message
saying which; it is not silently ignored, because a script that quietly
never runs is worse than one that fails to load.

Authority follows the file's location, not the configuration: a script
inside the project is the operator's own and may rewrite anything, while
one that arrived with a plugin may add. Nothing in this struct can change
that, which is deliberate — it would otherwise be a field a plugin could
set for itself.

calls_per_turn.description: How many times it may run in a turn. Defaults to the carrier's.

path.description: Path to the script, relative to the project root or absolute.

point.description: Which extension point, by its catalog id.

timeout_ms.description: Wall clock for one call. Defaults to the carrier's own budget.

SessionSettings.description: The limits of a session over all its turns.

token_budget.description:
Maximum cumulative tokens a session may spend from when it was
created, counted as `turn.token_budget` is (input not read from the
cache, cache writes and output) over every turn — its delegates', the
calls made on their side, scheduled and goal turns included — and
across restarts. Each call is judged as under `turn.token_budget`,
its input estimated and taken off what is left; with less than 1024
remaining no call is sent, and the turn, and every turn after it,
ends with `budget_exceeded`. `None` = unlimited.

allow_shell.description:
Run skill dynamic-content-injection shell commands (`` !`cmd` `` and
fenced ` ```! ` blocks in `SKILL.md` bodies). Default: true. When
false, each such placeholder is replaced with
`[shell command execution disabled by policy]` instead of running.
A higher tier can set it back, except a project that is not trusted
(`app.trusted_projects`).

allow.description:
Variables passed through whatever the mode would do with them — in
`allowlist` mode the extra names to keep, in `inherit` mode a way to
hand one of the engine's own credentials (a provider's `api_key_env`,
a variable an MCP server's configuration reads) to every child on
purpose.

oneOf.description: The host's environment, minus the engine's own credentials.
Only the variables a shell needs to work, plus `allow`.

TaskTiers.description:
The tier each kind of model call asks for. The task types: `main` (the
conversation), `subagent` (sub-agents started without a model of their
own), `compact` (summarizing for compaction), `memory` (extracting
memories), `title` (naming a session), `web_search` (`WebSearch`) and
`web_fetch` (`WebFetch` reading a page — unset, `WebFetch` uses no model
and returns the page text).

web_fetch.description: Default unset: no model reads fetched pages.

enabled.description:
Gates whether `TeamCreate`/`TeamList`/`TeamDelete` are registered at
all for a session, and only in a scene whose `SceneSpec::supports_team`
is true. Default `false`: an always-registered tool puts its
`tool.prompt.md` "When to Use" section in every system prompt and its
`team`/`name` input fields in every `Agent` tool schema, whether or not
the operator ever intends to allow it. Flipping this only affects
sessions built after the change.

max_members.description:
Reclaim policy for persistent team members (`Agent` tool's
`team_name`+`name` mode): total pool size across a session. Past it the
oldest-idle members are stopped (never an `Active` one), just enough to
be back at the cap. `0` turns persistent members off: such a call is
refused; one-shot sub-agents are not affected.

member_idle_secs.description:
Reclaim policy for persistent team members: how long a member may sit
idle (no message since its last turn finished) before it is stopped on
its own, independent of the total-count cap above.

stage_concurrency.description:
Maximum number of `TeamCreate` sub-agents dispatched concurrently
within a single stage.

enabled.description:
Whether sessions record a telemetry transcript.

Defaults to **on**: a session writes one JSONL file per session under
`<local_data_dir>/telemetry/`, which is what makes a run debuggable
after the fact (tool calls, permission decisions, turn costs).

otlp_endpoint.description:
OTLP endpoint telemetry events are exported to. Unset, the
`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` environment variable is used; neither
means no export. Only a build with the `otel` feature exports — any
other logs a warning when this is set.

Tier.description:
A model tier. Tasks and sessions ask for a tier; each provider says which
of its models serves it.

Tiers.description: Which of a provider's models serves each tier, as written.

max_model_calls.description:
Ceiling on LLM round trips in one turn, before the turn ends with
`stop_reason: "max_turns"`.

This is a runaway guard, not a task budget. Every comparable agent
runtime treats it that way and lands in the same range — the OpenAI
Agents SDK defaults `max_turns` to 10, LangGraph's `recursion_limit`
to 25, LangChain's `max_iterations` to 15. A long task is meant to be
served by compaction, delegation and resuming, not by a high ceiling:
raising this does not rescue an agent stuck in a loop, it only buys
the loop more iterations before it stops.

Raise it deliberately for a genuinely long single turn. Nothing here
detects a *lack of progress* — a model repeating the same failing
tool call burns the whole allowance either way.

parallel_tools.description: How many tool calls of one model reply run at once.

token_budget.description:
Maximum cumulative tokens (input not read from the cache, cache writes
and output, as provider quotas count them) one
turn may spend, its delegates included: every model call of the turn
and of the sub-agents and team members it starts or hands work to —
a background sub-agent's after the turn has ended too — counts toward
one total, hook model calls too. Before each call its input not
expected from the cache is estimated and taken off what is left; the
call asks for no more output than remains, and with less than 1024
remaining it is not sent. The turn ends with `budget_exceeded`, and a
delegate still running ends the same way before its next call. An
estimate, not a reservation: delegates running at once can each
overshoot by one call. `None` = unlimited.

Deliberately token-based, not a dollar figure: provider prices change
over time and per contract, so enforcing a dollar budget needs a
per-model price table that can silently drift out of date — a stale
or missing price makes the hard cap wrong in either direction. Token
counts come straight from the provider's own usage accounting on
every response, so there is nothing to keep in sync.

Vendor.description:
Who runs the endpoint. Decides what the protocol leaves open: how thinking
is switched on, whether reasoning goes back, how effort is spelled.

WebSettings.description: What the model's own web tools may reach.

allowed_domains.description:
Hosts the model may reach (`WebFetch`, `Ping`); a name also covers its
subdomains. Under `sandbox.network.mode: "allowlist"` it is the whole
list, but a sandboxed `Bash` / `Monitor` command reaches none of its
domains: the OS sandbox cannot filter by domain, and lets through only
localhost (macOS, when listed) or nothing (Linux). In every mode, a
host it names may be reached at an address on this machine or a
private network, which a model-directed request is otherwise refused —
write `127.0.0.1` here to let `WebFetch` reach a local server.

description:
One settings.json file, and what the settings tiers say once merged. Every
field is one a settings file can set; what loading them produced besides is
[`LoadedSettings`].

app.description: Read from the global tier only — see [`AppSettings`].

hooks.description:
Lifecycle hooks: an object from event name (`PreToolUse`,
`SessionStart`, … — `hooks::HookEvent`) to a list of hooks, each with
a `type` of `command`, `prompt`, `http` or `agent`. Tiers merge per
event: a tier that lists an event replaces the lower tiers' list for
it. An unknown event name is skipped with a warning; the rest still
apply. Format: `docs/hooks.md`.

permissions.description:
The permission mode, the allow / ask / deny rules, and how long a
permission prompt waits.

providers.description:
The model providers: each one's endpoint, models, tiers and quota.
Tiers add to the list rather than replace it; an id already defined
in a tier read earlier (global, scene, project — each tier's
`settings.local.json` after its `settings.json`) is ignored with a
warning. With none defined, the engine supplies `anthropic`: Anthropic's
API, keyed from `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or the
host, at `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` when set, every tier the daemon's
`--model`. Not read from a project that is not trusted.

scripts.description:
Scripts bound to extension points — see [`ScriptBinding`]. Empty by
default, and inert in a build without a script engine.
